Reliable. Responsible. Resilient. 
In a landscape shaped by surging energy demand, rigorous sustainability 
targets and shifting regulatory frameworks; power utilities must deliver 
seamlessly to support the nation’s growth aspirations. Torrent Power 
embodies this mandate through its guiding pillars: Reliable, Responsible and 
Resilient —values that drive every strategic decision and operational initiative.
Torrent Power’s commitment to reliability is evident in its integrated generation and distribution network. We understand 
that consistent and dependable power supply is crucial for the growth and prosperity of the communities we serve. By 
blending thermal plants, gas turbines and an expanding portfolio of solar and wind assets; we ensure uninterrupted power 
to major urban centres and industries. Our state-of-the-art infrastructure coupled with cutting-edge monitoring technologies 
and proactive maintenance regimes minimise outages; ensure that we are the most reliable power distribution licensee 
in the country. Our dedicated team works tirelessly to minimise disruptions and provide seamless service, reinforcing our 
reputation as a trusted energy provider.
Responsibility towards our environment, customers and society is deeply ingrained in our corporate ethos. The Company 
is accredited with various awards and certifications which demonstrate our strong commitment towards reliability, 
sustainability, quality and operational excellence. As a conscientious corporate citizen, Torrent Power champions 
environmental stewardship through significant investments in renewable energy, aligning with national decarbonisation 
goals. Our thermal facilities incorporate water-conservation systems and waste management practices, demonstrating 
our dedication to resource efficiency. Our digital touchpoints empower customers to manage their energy activities 
seamlessly. Beyond infrastructure, our community outreach programs and transparent stakeholder dialogues reinforce our 
ethical commitment to the regions we serve. Our corporate social responsibility programs focus on uplifting communities, 
enhancing education, and supporting healthcare initiatives. By integrating ethical practices into our business model, we 
strive to create a positive impact and contribute to a greener, and more equitable future.
Our resilience lies in the capacity to adapt to a dynamic external environment, market fluctuations and technological 
breakthroughs. A robust risk management framework and flexible business models enable us to navigate through regulatory 
changes, address climate-related risks, explore new markets and respond to unforeseen events. This agility not only secures 
stable returns for investors but also maintains operational excellence and insulates consumers from supply disruptions. 
We continuously invest in our people, processes and technology to build a resilient organisation capable of withstanding 
and thriving amidst adversity.
By weaving reliability, responsibility and resilience into its DNA, we, at Torrent Power, fortify energy security for millions 
and catalyse economic growth across its service areas. This holistic approach to power delivery not only supports India’s 
ongoing development but also cements Torrent Power’s reputation as a forward-looking leader in the nation’s dynamic 
energy transition.

Torrent Power Limited (referred to as ‘Torrent Power’, ‘Our Company’, or ‘We’) 
presents the fourth Integrated Annual Report for the Financial Year 2024-25 
(FY25). This Integrated Report highlights sustainable impact we have on our 
stakeholders, balancing needs of people and planet while ensuring profitability 
of our operations. We believe it provides transparent and balanced account 
of how we create and preserve value for all our stakeholders.
Frameworks, Guidelines and Standards
The report is presented in adherence to the requirements 
of IR framework developed by IIRC (International Integrated 
Reporting Council), now part of the IFRS Foundation.  
The sustainability performance metrics aligns to the ‘Core’ 
option of the Global Reporting Initiative (GRI). Further, 
this report is prepared in reference or accordance with 
various Indian as well as global frameworks and standards 
including the Sustainability Accounting Standards Board 
(SASB), United Nations Sustainable Development Goals 
(UN SDGs), United Nations Global Compact (UNGC) and 
National Guidelines for Responsible Business Conduct 
(NGRBC). The report also provides linkage to various 
parameters of such frameworks against GRI indicators.
The statutory sections of the report have been developed 
in compliance with:
 ®Companies Act, 2013 (including rules made thereunder)
 ®Indian Accounting Standards 
 ®Securities and Exchange Board of India (Listing 
Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) 
Regulations, 2015 
 ®Secretarial Standards issued by The Institute of 
Company Secretaries of India
Reporting Period
The information presented in this report pertains to the 
period between April 1, 2024 to March 31, 2025.About the Report
Reporting Boundary and Scope
The report provides a comprehensive overview of 
all operations of Torrent Power and its subsidiaries, 
including Thermal and Renewable Generation, Licensed 
and Franchised Distribution, Transmission and Cables 
Manufacturing business (till sale of cables manufacturing 
business i.e. October 16, 2024).
Responsibility Statement
The Board of Directors acknowledges its accountability for 
the integrity and completeness of the report, including its 
presentation, which is guided by the IR framework.
Feedback

our sustainability practices and reporting standards 
in collaboration with our stakeholders. Kindly 
direct your valuable feedback and suggestions to:

Forward-looking Statements
Certain statements in this report may be forward-looking. 
Actual outcomes may vary from those expressed or implied. 
The Company assumes no responsibility to publicly amend, 
modify, update or revise any such statements based on 
subsequent developments, information or events.

behind a world rich in flora and fauna and rich in time 
tested values and ideals and above all rich in social

to leadership. As we are what we repeatedly do, 
excellence then is not an act, but a habit.Fairness with Care
Harnessing equality
Fairness and Care towards all fellow members are 
inextricably linked. Weaving the threads of equality,

Leading India’s Energy TransitionCHAIRMAN’S MESSAGE
respectively, highlighting the momentum towards a clean 
energy future.
To support this energy shift, India is significantly expanding 
its transmission network, planning over 1,91,000 circuit 
kilometres lines and 1,270 GVA transformation capacity 
by 2032. Policy frameworks are evolving in parallel, with 
incentives for rooftop solar under the PM Surya Ghar Yojana, 
and targeted support for green hydrogen, battery storage, 
and domestic manufacturing under the Union Budget 
2025–26. The rapid advancement of electric mobility, with 
~30% EV penetration targeted by 2030, is further driving 
demand for decentralised generation, grid flexibility, and 
energy storage. Simultaneously, the Country’s data centre 
landscape is undergoing rapid expansion, with operational 
capacity expected to reach 2,000–2,100 MW by March 2027 
further driving power demand and reinforcing the need for 
resilient and sustainable energy systems. 
Against this dynamic backdrop, our operating environment 
is shaped by rising demand, evolving policies, and  
technological progress. Throughout FY25, we focused on 
investing in clean energy, ensuring reliability across thermal 
assets, strengthening grid and network capabilities, and 
managing capital prudently. Torrent Power’s integrated 
presence across generation, transmission, and distribution 
enables us to respond to sectoral shifts with agility, 
foresight, and execution strength. The year reinforced the 
relevance of our strategy and the trust reposed in us by 
our stakeholders.
Operational and Financial Performance
Torrent Power delivered a strong performance across its 
generation, transmission, and distribution businesses in 
FY25, driven by disciplined execution, strategic investments, 
and alignment with India’s energy transition goals. The 
Company’s total generation capacity including under 
construction capacity stood at ~7,992 MWp, with renewable 
energy capacity at ~4,900 MWp i.e. ~61% of total capacity. 
Our gas-based thermal plants — SUGEN, UNOSUGEN, and 
DGEN — operated at modest levels owing to reduced offtake 
from long-term beneficiaries and elevated gas prices, which 
was partially offset by increased merchant and bilateral 
sales, including NVVN tenders and Section 11 imposed by 
government for gas-based power plants. These plants played 
a crucial role in meeting peak demand and maintaining grid 
stability. The AMGEN coal-based plant continued to meet 
supply obligations in the licensed distribution area.
In renewables, we commissioned a 510 MWp solar 
capacity, bringing total operational renewable capacity

Navigating the Power Sector
India’s energy sector is undergoing a paradigm 
transformation, driven by rapid economic growth, 
urbanisation, steadily rising electricity demand and a low 
carbon future. To meet this need, India has set ambitious 
targets: 500 GW of non-fossil fuel capacity by 2030 and 
net-zero emissions by 2070. As of March 2025, total 
installed capacity reached ~475 GW, with solar contributing 
~106 GW, wind and hydropower at ~50 GW and ~48 GW

The Company reported a Profit Before Tax (PBT) of ₹3,253

Furthermore, Total Comprehensive Income (TCI) included

amounting to ₹637 Crore resulting in substantial 63% year-
on-year TCI growth i.e. ₹1,177 Crore. The Company has 
consistently delivered superior Return on Equity and Return 
on Capital Employed over peers.
During the year, capital expenditure totalled ₹4,388 Crore, 
with over 50% strategically allocated to the development 
of clean energy infrastructure. This underscores our 
continued commitment to expanding clean energy capacity, 
strengthening transmission systems, and modernising 
distribution networks reinforcing our commitment to 
sustainable energy future.
We continue to maintain a conservative capital structure, 
strong liquidity, and a clear focus on cost efficiency. 
Margin stability was ensured through disciplined project 
execution, digital adoption, and reliable cash flows from 
regulated operations.to  1,746 MWp.  The under-development pipeline now 
stands at 3,154 MWp, backed by a committed investment 
of over ₹20,000 Crore spanning across Wind, Solar, Hybrid, 
and Commercial & Industrial (C&I) segments. Additionally, 
we signed major agreement with Maharashtra State 
Electricity Distribution Company Limited (MSEDCL) to 
supply 2,000 MW/ 16,000 MWh through Pumped Hydro 
Storage, positioning Torrent Power as an early leader in 
long-duration storage infrastructure. 
In the transmission segment, we are executing two key 
renewable power evacuation projects — one in Khavda, 
Gujarat, and another in Solapur, Maharashtra — with a 
combined investment of approximately ₹1,300 Crore. 
Our distribution business continued to deliver benchmark 
efficiency, serving over 4.2 million customers across three 
states and one Union Territory, while maintaining one of 
the lowest distribution loss levels in the country. The 
Distribution business demonstrated exemplary operational 
performance, achieving distribution loss of 2.34% in our 
licensed areas, which is the lowest in the country and at 
par with international best practices. This accomplishment 
reflects our sustained focus on operational excellence 
and efficiency. In our franchised distribution areas, Agra 
stands out as a noteworthy success story, where Aggregate 
Technical & Commercial (AT&C) losses have been brought 
down to a record low of 6.94% this year, a remarkable 
turnaround from 58.77% at the time of takeover in 2010, 
highlighting our long-term commitment to system reliability, 
loss reduction, and customer-centric service delivery. 
Torrent Power’s licensed distribution areas in Ahmedabad, 
Surat, and Dahej received the prestigious 6-Star EFQM 
rating, a mark of excellence in reliability, digital integration, 
sustainable performance, and customer service.  
We continue to enhance customer experience through 
improved supply reliability and sustained reduction in 
distribution losses. By leveraging our demonstrated expertise 
in distribution operations, we are investing consistently to 
improve network quality and operational responsiveness. 
On the financial front, Torrent Power achieved a significant 
milestone by successfully completing its maiden equity raise 
of ₹3,500 Crore through a Qualified Institutional Placement 
(QIP) marking the Torrent Group’s first equity issuance in 
over three decades. This offering received an overwhelming 
response, with a 4x oversubscription, reflecting strong 
confidence from both Foreign and Domestic Institutional

Our Next Phase of Growth
We aim to achieve 10 GW of renewable capacity by 2030, 
backed by an under-construction capacity of more than 
3 GWp. Our strategy is built on a diversified portfolio, 
encompassing utility-scale solar, wind, hybrid, round-
the-clock projects and supplying renewable power to C&I 
customers. Additionally, we are evaluating opportunities in 
green hydrogen and green ammonia to complement our 
clean energy initiatives.
To enhance grid flexibility and ensure firm renewable 
power delivery, we are exploring Pumped Hydro Storage 
opportunities in Maharashtra and Uttar Pradesh with a 
cumulative potential capacity of ~8.4 GW, of which 2 GW 
is already secured through firm agreement. Our goal is to 
build a future-ready energy portfolio that balances energy 
security, commercial viability, and sustainability. Thermal 
power remains essential for India’s energy security and 
grid stability. Given current power demand dynamics, we 
are also prioritising thermal generation. In particular, our 
gas-based plants are expected to operate at healthy Plant 
Load Factors, supporting grid reliability during periods of 
high peak demand and renewable intermittency. We are 
also actively considering to develop coal-based thermal 
power projects to participate in competitive bids being 
floated by state DISCOMs, as well as secure power supply 
for our distribution business, reinforcing our commitment 
to meeting the country’s growing energy demands with 
reliable and scalable solutions.On the infrastructure front, we continue to enhance 
customer experience by improving supply reliability and 
reducing distribution losses in our existing distribution 
areas. We are equally focused on expanding the reach of 
our distribution business by pursuing new opportunities in 
distribution privatisation, parallel licenses and franchisee 
models. Our strong track record in efficient, customer-
centric operations positions us well to create value across 
a broader footprint.
In transmission, we continue to pursue both brownfield 
and greenfield expansions. We plan to continue to actively 
participate in competitive bidding for both inter-state and 
intra-state transmission projects to facilitate the growing 
integration of renewable energy into the national grid.
As we pursue these opportunities, we remain committed 
to upholding the highest standards of ESG performance. 
Sustainability, transparency, and responsible stewardship 
will continue to guide our decisions ensuring long-term 
value-creation for our stakeholders.

Empowering India’s Growth CORPORATE PORTRAIT
We have a strong presence across the entire energy value chain—from power 
generation and transmission to distribution, ensuring operational excellence 
and uninterrupted power supply. With a diverse portfolio of renewable and 
thermal energy, we provide reliable, affordable, and sustainable electricity to 
more than 4 million customers. 
As an integrated power utility, we remain committed to 
fostering innovation, optimising operational efficiency, and 
placing customer satisfaction at the heart of our efforts to 
drive sustainable and resilient business growth.
Our robust and strategically positioned distribution 
network—spanning both licensed and franchised areas—
ensures efficient service delivery across urban and 
industrial centres, minimising distribution losses and 
strengthening overall system resilience. Our state-of-the-
art gas-based power generation plants ensure grid stability. In alignment with the evolving energy landscape, we have 
significantly expanded our renewable energy portfolio to 
nearly 5 GWp, which now constitutes over 60% of our total 
generation capacity. 
Furthering our commitment to clean energy, the Company 
is planning to develop approximately 8.4 GW of Pumped 
Storage Hydro projects across Uttar Pradesh and 
Maharashtra, reinforcing our role in shaping a sustainable 
energy future.

BUSINESS REVIEW
Powering India’s Progress
We are one of India’s leading private sector integrated power utility companies 
with an established presence across power generation, transmission and

Thermal Generation
Our thermal generation capacity of 3,092 MW comprises 
2,730 MW from natural gas-based plants and 362 MW 
from coal-based plant, accounting for ~88% and ~12% of 
our total thermal capacity, respectively. We continuously 
enhance our infrastructure to ensure seamless operations

evolving energy market.    
Coal-based Generation
Our coal-based generation facility in Ahmedabad, 
Gujarat—a 362 MW AMGEN power plant, helps to meet the 
demand of our licensed distribution operations. It operates 
on approximately 70:30 domestic-to-imported coal mix, 
ensuring both fuel efficiency and cost-effectiveness.
Operational for over three decades, the plant has consistently 
driven exceptional performance, maximising plant 
availability, boosting operational efficiency, and mitigating 
environmental impact through strategic maintenance, 
technology upgrades, and process enhancements. 
Regulated by the Gujarat Electricity Regulatory Commission 
(GERC), AMGEN operates under a cost-plus post-tax 
Return on Equity (RoE) / Return on Capital Employed (RoCE) 
as per applicable regulations. This framework ensures 
stability, incentivises efficient operations, and maintains 
financial viability.
During FY25, AMGEN successfully completed a major 
turbine overhaul at Unit D, resulting in improved operational efficiency and enhanced reliability. This strategic upgrade 
will deliver significant long-term benefit, however, it led to a 
temporary reduction in plant availability for the year.

Enhancing Operational Efficiency and Reliability in Renewable Plants
We continue to improve the performance of our 
renewable assets through advanced monitoring, 
predictive maintenance, and technological upgrades 
by taking below initiatives:
 ®Centralised Remote Monitoring:  A SCADA-enabled 
system at SUGEN tracks real-time performance of 
solar and wind assets, enabling predictive analysis 
and condition-based maintenance to optimise 
generation efficiency.
 ®Real-time Condition Monitoring System: An 
online real time drive train vibration monitoring 
system has been installed in 13 of our Wind Turbines, 
which assists with the early detection of major 
component failures.
 ®Drone-based Inspections:  Drones for transmission 
line and wind turbine blade inspections have been 
deployed, enabling early fault detection and timely 
corrective actions to minimise generation loss and 
enhance turbine availability. 
 ®Robotic and Advanced Cleaning Methods:  
Implemented robotic solar module cleaning at 
various solar sites, reducing soiling loss and 
conserving water, complemented by hybrid dry and 
wet cleaning methods at other locations.  ®Proactive Diagnostic Techniques and SCADA 
data analysis: Adopted drone thermography, 
transformer oil analysis, and equipment testing to 
ensure early fault detection and timely intervention, 
enhancing the reliability of solar plants. Used SCADA 
data to identify and rectify string faults in solar plants 
and manage power curve deviations in wind turbines, 
optimising performance and preventing outages.
 ®RTV Silicone Coating:  Applied Room Temperature 
Vulcanising (RTV) silicone coating to MV panels at 
some of our solar and wind sites to mitigate insulation 
failures caused by moisture and dust, enhancing 
electrical insulation and system durability. 
 ®Self O&M:  Transitioned to self-operation and 
maintenance (O&M) at various sites, improving 
response times and asset availability. Onboarded 
local vendors for component repairs, reducing 
downtime and maintenance costs, and ensuring 
quicker resolution of issues. 
 ®Module Performance Optimisation:  Proactively 
identified underperforming modules through IV 
curve/VOC test and such modules are being 
reshuffled to one location/string or replaced to 
improve generation.

Drivetrain Grounding System Installation, Jam-Khambhaliya
Our 116.1 MW wind farm with 43 Wind Turbine 
Generators (WTGs), at Jam-Khambhaliya, 
encountered recurring issues with drivetrain - the 
part of the wind turbine that transfers energy from 
the blades to the generator. These issues were 
mainly caused by stray electrical currents from 
lightning and static electricity, which damaged 
critical components like the main bearings. This 
led to frequent breakdowns, more maintenance, 
and higher costs. To address these issues, we 
implemented a drivetrain grounding system 
with objectives as - Divert and Neutralise Stray 
Electrical Currents; Static Charge Minimisation; special attention to safeguarding the main bearings, 
preventing electrical erosion and extending the 
operational life of these critical parts. 
Key benefits include - Enhanced reliability, 
extended component life, reduced downtime and 
operational costs, optimised performance, and 
standards compliance.
Through this proactive approach, we have 
demonstrated our commitment to improving the 
performance and sustainability, ensuring reliable 
operations for stakeholders.

Pumped Storage Project and Green 
Hydrogen
The Company is reinforcing its commitment to grid stability 
and renewable integration through development of a 3,000 
MW / 18,000 MWh Pumped Storage Project (PSP) in Raigad, 
Maharashtra. A 40-year Energy Storage Facility Agreement 
for 2,000 MW has been signed with Maharashtra State 
Electricity Distribution Company Limited (MSEDCL), while 
the remaining 1,000 MW is being developed as merchant 
capacity. The Company has secured in-principle allotments 
for PSP sites in Maharashtra and Uttar Pradesh, with a 
capacity of 8,350 MW across four locations.
In parallel, the Company is exploring investment 
opportunities in Green Hydrogen sector. The Company 
was awarded Production Linked Incentive (PLI) under 
MNRE’s SIGHT scheme for producing 18,000 TPA of Green 
Hydrogen. The Company has received in-principle approval 
for ~17,000 acres of land in Gujarat for a production facility 
integrated with renewable energy. A pilot project blending 
~2% Green Hydrogen into the city gas network in Gorakhpur 
marks a key milestone in this journey.

Licensed Distribution Assets
We are the licensed operator for electricity distribution 
in several regions of Gujarat, including Ahmedabad, 
Gandhinagar, Surat, Dahej SEZ, Dholera SIR and Mandal 
Bechraji SIR and in the union territory of Dadra & Nagar 
Haveli and Daman & Diu (DNH&DD), covering an aggregate 
area of ~2,050 sq. km. The licensed distribution business 
of our Company in the state of Gujarat is regulated by 
Gujarat Electricity Regulatory Commission (GERC) and in 
union territory of DNH&DD by Joint Electricity Regulatory 
Commission (JERC), which allows cost plus post-tax 
Return on Equity/Return on Capital Employed, along with 
performance incentives as part of a regulated tariff structure. 
Our distribution losses at licensed distribution areas are 
one of the lowest globally and well below the normative 
levels, reflective of the highest standards of operations. Distribution

In Ahmedabad, the traditional electrical distribution 
setup required separate installations for the 11 kV 
Ring Main Unit (RMU) and metering panel, leading to 
increased complexity in installation, maintenance, and 
space utilisation. Managing multiple components posed 
challenges in achieving optimal safety, reliability and 
cost efficiency.
To modernise the network, we designed and developed 
a new compact switchgear integrating the 11 kV RMU 
and metering panel into a single unit. The switchgear 
was deployed after undergoing  rigorous type testing at 
the Electrical Research and Development Association 
(ERDA) to ensure compliance with safety and 
regulatory standards.

 ®Optimised Space Utilisation:  Integration of RMU

Optimising Power Distribution in Bhiwandi and SMK
To improve efficiency, reliability and response time in Bhiwandi and Shil Mumbra-Kalwa (SMK) franchise areas,  
we have implemented several key initiatives:
 ® Introduction of Latitude-Longitude (Lat -Long) in 
Field Force Application (FFA)
  Previously, our teams relied on AutoCAD maps and 
manual coordination to locate services, which often 
resulted in delays. To address this, we integrated 
latitude-longitude data into the Field Force Application 
(FFA), enabling real-time tracking via Google Maps. 
This integration has led to faster response times in 
service resolution, improved accuracy in locating 
network service locations, and increased operational 
efficiency through real-time navigation.
 ® System Diagram Book (SDB) Distribution
  High Tension (HT) Feeder Single Line Diagrams (SLD) 
were previously only available digitally, complicating 
access during network outages or emergencies.  
To ensure seamless operations, we developed a 
physical feeder SDB handbook that consolidates 
key HT network details, including isolation points, 
transformer data, and switching station diagrams. This handbook provides a simplified, quick-reference 
guide, improves response times in fault management, 
supports disaster recovery operations, and helps new 
team members quickly understand HT networks.
 ® Reliability Improvement through Feeder 
Interlinking and SCADA
  To improve power restoration efficiency and network 
reliability, we transitioned from manual switchgear 
operations and fault-prone feeder networks to 
SCADA-controlled systems, including RMUs and 
auto-reclosers. Feeder interlinking was introduced for 
optimised load management, and outdated SCADA 
links were replaced. These upgrades have enabled 
faster fault detection and resolution, reduced SAIFI 
and SAIDI indices, and achieved 100% SCADA 
availability, significantly minimising outage frequency 
and duration.FY21 FY22 FY23 FY24 FY25Distribution Loss (%)

Transition to VRLA Batteries for Reliable 
Power Backup
To modernise backup power systems and reduce 
maintenance efforts, we replaced conventional lead-
acid batteries with advanced Valve Regulated Lead 
Acid (VRLA) batteries across key substations in the 
SMK distribution area.
Earlier, substations used flooded lead-acid batteries 
for auxiliary power supply to power protection 
and control systems. These required frequent 
maintenance, occupied significant space, and posed 
safety and environmental risks, including hydrogen 
emissions and acid leaks.
In May 2024, the outdated batteries were replaced 
with VRLA AGM batteries. With a sealed design, 
maintenance-free operations and longer life 
expectancy, these batteries optimise efficiency 
and reliability. 
Key Outcomes
 ®Improved System Reliability: Stable voltage 
output minimises system failures during 
power transition.
 ®Lower Operational Costs: Extended battery 
lifespan reduces replacement frequency and 
maintenance expenses.
 ®Optimised Space Utilisation:  No need for spill 
containment or as much ventilation systems, 
freeing up space for future expansion.
 ®Enhanced Workplace Safety : Eliminates risks of 
acid spills enhancing personal safety and reducing 
environmental hazards.
 ®Environmental Compliance: Meets stringent 
environmental regulations with reduced 
gas emissions.
High Capacity Compact- VRLA Batteries
Lead Acid-Batteries
Way Forward
The Company continues to strengthen its licensed and 
franchised distribution operations by leveraging advanced 
technology and automation to meet rising demand and

distribution losses, the Company is well-positioned

to delicense electricity distribution and promote open

around franchised operations enhances its prospects 
for future franchise or parallel licensee opportunities.

We continue to strengthen our transmission infrastructure 
to facilitate efficient power evacuation and grid stability. We 
transmit power from our gas-based plants to various off-
take centres through 128 km of 220 kV double-circuit lines 
and 355 km of 400 kV double-circuit lines. Part of these 
transmission lines are operated through our subsidiary, 
Torrent Power Grid Limited (TPGL). We hold a 74% stake in 
Torrent Power Grid Limited, with the remaining 26% held by 
Power Grid Corporation of India Limited. The transmission 
lines under Torrent Power Grid Limited’s operations are 
governed by CERC Tariff Regulations, which allow for a 
post-tax ROE of 15.50%, plus additional incentives.
Two key transmission projects, supporting renewable 
energy integration are currently under development by 
the Company. The Khavda Project  in Gujarat, awarded in FY23, involves 
the evacuation of 4.5 GW of renewable energy through a 60 
km 400 kV double-circuit transmission line and associated 
bay upgradation. The project operates under a regulated 
tariff framework as per the CERC (Terms and Conditions 
of Tariff) Regulations, 2024, ensuring a cost-plus post-tax 
Return on Equity (RoE) of 15%. The project is scheduled to 
be commissioned  in FY26.
The Solapur Project in Maharashtra, is aimed to facilitate 
power evacuation from 1.5 GW renewable power projects 
in Solapur SEZ, Maharashtra. The project was secured in 
FY24 under the Tariff Based Competitive Bidding (TBCB) 
process, is being developed on a Build, Own, Operate, 
and Transfer (BOOT) basis for a 35-year period. The scope 
includes a 44 km 400 kV double-circuit transmission line, 
Transmission Tower, Ahmedabad

Securing the Digital EdgeCYBERSECURITY AND DISASTER MANAGEMENT 
At Torrent Power, we prioritise cybersecurity and risk preparedness to 
ensure stability, continuity, and strong defence against evolving threats in 
a technology-driven industry. By adopting advanced security frameworks, 
maintaining constant vigilance, and adhering to global best practices, we 
safeguard critical assets and uphold long-term trust in an inter-connected  
world. This comprehensive strategy keeps us leading in innovation, 
empowering our teams, enhancing the efficiency and effectiveness of our 
operations, and delivering an exceptional experience for our customers.
Fortifying Cyber Resilience
We are committed to enhancing our operational efficiency, 
customer experience, and innovation through digital and 
technological advancements. Our IT infrastructure, certified 
under ISO 27001:2022 (Information Security Management 
System), adheres to the latest information security best 
practices, ensuring comprehensive coverage for information 
security, cybersecurity, and privacy protection. 
Our dedicated Cybersecurity Cell, led by the Chief 
Information Security Officer (CISO), oversees Cybersecurity governance, coordination, and strategic planning. The 
cell provides engineering support and monitors risk 
posture using advanced processes and technology. We 
are implementing 24/7 Security Operations Centre (SOC) 
to continuously monitor and respond to cyber threats. 
Additionally, a Cyber Crisis Management Plan (CCMP), 
approved by the Ministry of Power, Government of India, 
is in place for our Generation and Distribution businesses. 
We diligently comply with the Central Electricity Authority 
(CEA)/CERT-In Advisory to maintain robust cybersecurity 
protocols against suspicious domains.

External Surface Monitoring for Security Rating (Score) and Vendor Risk Management
The Company faced challenges due to limited visibility into 
security risks affecting our external applications, network, 
and IT systems. In addition, the security practices of key 
vendors, including those using SaaS platforms, were not 
being adequately monitored or evaluated.

to monitor, measure, and control the security rating of 
external surface exposure, including breaches, attacks,

 ®Continuous Monitoring:  The initiative provides 
continuous monitoring and notification of external

 ®Vendor Risk Management:  The Vendor Risk Matrix

Leveraging Technology in Operations
At Torrent Power, we are committed to harnessing advanced 
technology to enhance our operations and ensure regulatory 
compliance. Our fully digitalised processes, supported by 
an advanced Enterprise Content Management system, 
exemplify our dedication to efficiency and innovation.
Generation
Our generation business, a cornerstone of our organisation, 
relies on cutting-edge technology to maintain asset 
efficiency and deliver continuous value to stakeholders. 
We utilise advanced analytics and real-time monitoring 
systems to optimise power plant performance, ensuring 
maximum output and minimal downtime. Recent upgrades 
to our Distributed Control System (DCS) and generator 
excitation systems with the latest technology mod ules, 
have enhanced operational flexibility, reduced component 
requirements, and ensured cybersecurity compliance.
Distribution
We have implemented various digital and technological 
solutions to enhance our distribution network.  
Our SCADA system manage all EHV substations and 
feeders. We are currently integrating an Advanced 
Distribution Management System (ADMS) to enable 
remote operations and optimise network performance. 
Our automatic meter reading infrastructure, utilising GPRS 
and Nb-IoT, provides real-time energy consumption data. 
We are also piloting Advanced Metering Infrastructure 
(AMI) with Smart Meters and advanced technology 
platforms. Additionally, our GIS-based interface improves 
functional efficiency and enables remote operations. Our 
mobile-based Field Force Application (FFA) supports 
field engineers in monitoring activities and capturing data 
digitally, enhancing operational efficiency and promoting 
paperless operations.
Customer Service Enhancements
To enhance customer experience, we have introduced 
mobile notifications for outages and updates, a mobile 
application, customer portal, and various initiatives to 
improve billing accuracy and consumer satisfaction. 
Additionally, we are updating bill formats to include 
QR codes for easier payment. Furthermore, we are 
implementing multilingual AI chatbots to provide efficient 
and personalised customer service.
Innovation and AI Integration
We leverage open-source platforms and DevOps 
practices to ensure seamless integration and delivery of 
IT applications. By utilising low code/no code platforms, 
we streamline application development efficiently.  
Our centralised deployment of Zabbix and OpenNMS 
facilitates comprehensive network monitoring and timely notifications in case of outages. To enhance daily 
operations, we incorporate AI through Microsoft Copilot. 
Furthermore, our Enterprise Content Management System 
bolsters knowledge management and collaboration, while 
SAP Analytics Cloud and Power BI offer robust data analysis 
and reporting capabilities.
By leveraging these advanced technologies, the Company 
is well-positioned to navigate industry complexities, grow 
sustainably, and meet the increasing power demand of 
the country.
Disaster Management and Business 
Continuity
In recognition of the inherent risks of disasters, we have 
developed a comprehensive recovery plan to ensure swift 
resumption of business operations. Our efforts focus 
on building robust and scalable disaster management 
capabilities, leveraging IT to quickly restore access 
to power, connectivity, data, hardware, software, and 
network equipment. Our licensed distribution areas of 
Ahmedabad, Surat and Dahej have ISO 22301 (Business 
Continuity Management System) certification, highlighting 
our dedication to robust disaster management.
To ensure robust disaster management and business 
continuity, we have implemented the following measures:
 ® High Availability Architecture:  Ensures business 
continuity  despite component or system failure.
 ®Robust Disaster Recovery Infrastructure:   
Our Disaster Recovery (DR) site is strategically located 
in different seismic zones, and we conduct regular DC-
DR drills to monitor key performance indicators for 
business continuity.
 ®Robust Disaster Management Capabilities: 
Designed for quick restoration of critical systems with 
minimal downtime.
 ®Advanced Backup and Recovery System:  
Implemented advanced backup systems, including air-
gapped backups (under implementation), to recover 
from ransomware. Any abnormal data behaviour is 
promptly notified, and previously backed-up data is 
made available.
 ®Defined Communication Protocols:  Streamlined 
reporting mechanisms for immediate action.
 ®Specialised Response Teams:  Dedicated teams for 
cybersecurity incidents and disaster recovery.
Our framework combines risk assessment, rapid response, 
and technology to ensure operational resilience and 
continuity during disasters.

  10,724Capital Structure and Debt Management
FY25 has been a transformative year for Torrent Power, 
characterised by notable financial accomplishments and 
strategic advancements. A key milestone was the successful 
execution of our maiden Qualified Institutions Placement 
(QIP), through which the Company raised ₹3,500 Crore. 
This transaction not only marked Torrent Power’s first equity 
issuance but also represented the Torrent Group’s first equity 
raise in over thirty years. The offering was oversubscribed 
four times, reflecting strong investor confidence in the 
Company’s fundamentals, strategic direction, and growth 
potential. Participation from leading global and domestic 
institutions underscores our credibility and reinforces our 
position as a key player in India’s power sector. The funds raised through QIP enabled us to de-leverage and further 
strengthen our balance sheet, enabling us to accelerate the 
expansion in key strategic projects, driving future growth 
and enhancing our market position.
In addition to equity, we also prioritise prudent debt 
management to maintain a strong financial position.  
We successfully improved our Long-term Debt-to-Equity 
ratio from 0.88 in FY24 to 0.46 in FY25 and our Net Debt-
to-EBITDA from 2.25 in FY24 to 1.41 in FY25, reflecting our 
robust financial standing. Our interest service coverage ratio 
reached 5.50x, ensuring adequate liquidity. Furthermore, 
we continue to optimise our debt portfolio by balancing 
short-term and long-term borrowing, securing low-cost debt 
financing, and exploring refinancing opportunities.

CAGR  9.19 % Robust Operational Performance 
Driven by sustained economic momentum, power demand 
remained robust throughout FY25. The Company reported 
revenue of ₹29,165 Crore, marking a 7.3% increase over 
₹27,183 Crore in FY24. Profit Before Tax (PBT) rose sharply 
by 26% year-on-year to ₹3,253 Crore, primarily supported 
by improved margins in gas-based power generation. 
Operational efficiencies in the distribution segment—such 
as higher volumes, reduced technical and commercial 
losses, and ROE on newly added capital investments—also 
contributed significantly to this growth.
Additionally, one-time gains from the sale of non-current 
investments further supported profitability. However, these 
gains were partially offset by subdued performance in the 
renewable energy portfolio, impacted by unfavourable 
weather conditions and the stabilisation phase of newly 
commissioned solar assets.
This strong performance was further enhanced by a 
reduction in tax expenses, primarily due to a one-time, non-
cash reversal of deferred tax liabilities amounting to ₹637 
Crore. This lead the Total Comprehensive Income (TCI) to 
surge by 63% year-on-year, reflecting an increase of ₹1,177 
Crore over the previous fiscal. Strong Liquidity and Cash Flow
Our robust liquidity framework enables us to maintain

Talent Acquisition
We believe that a skilled, engaged and future-ready workforce is essential for driving innovation and delivering value across 
our operations. Our talent acquisition strategy is built on a multi-faceted approach that combines robust recruitment 
practices, strong employer branding, and a seamless onboarding experience to attract and retain top professionals.
Our Approach to Hiring
Comprehensive Recruitment Process
We follow a structured and objective recruitment process, 
evaluating candidates based on technical expertise, growth 
potential, and cultural alignment. We also have a Relative 
Recruitment Policy which encourages employee referrals, 
allowing our team members to recommend candidates who 
are more likely to grow within our ecosystem.
Unified Recruitment Drives
We conduct coordinated recruitment campaigns across 
business units to ensure efficiency, consistency, and wider 
reach, enabling us to tap into a diverse and skilled talent 
pool while maintaining high standards in evaluation.
Employer Branding
Our reputation as a preferred employer is built through our 
corporate website, job portals, social media platforms, and 
authentic employee testimonials. This enables us to project 
a compelling employee value proposition that resonates 
with top talent across the industry.Proactive Talent Pipeline
We actively maintain strong relationships with high-
potential candidates, even when immediate opportunities 
are not available. This forward-looking strategy ensures 
we are well-prepared for future business needs and 
succession requirements.
Commitment to a Smooth Hiring Experience
We prioritise transparency and candidate experience, 
with clear communication, timely feedback, and prompt 
resolution of any queries during the hiring process. This 
creates a positive first impression and reinforces our 
professional standards.
Seamless Onboarding
Our onboarding process is designed to integrate new 
employees effectively and foster early engagement. New 
hires receive personalised welcome communication, joining 
kits, and participate in structured induction programs, 
including cross-functional introductions and cultural 
orientation. We ensure they are well-equipped, confident, 
and connected from day one.

Training and Development 
We emphasise role-aligned continuous learning to empower our employees and enhance organisational performance. Our 
learning philosophy focuses on strengthening individual capabilities through targeted training, leadership grooming, and 
succession readiness.
Learning Philosophy
Continuous learning is embedded in our culture, 
with programs tailored to individual roles and 
aspirations. We leverage structured platforms and 
competency frameworks to guide this journey.At Torrent, training programs are developed through a 
comprehensive Training Needs Identification (TNI) process, 
which evaluates employee requirements across technical 
skills, behavioural competencies, functional knowledge, 
health, safety, environment and leadership development. 
Complemented by job rotation and enlargement initiatives, 
this approach enhances employee engagement and skill 
diversity. Together, these initiatives ensure that learning and 
development efforts not only support individual growth but 
also align closely with the organisation’s strategic goals. 
During the year E-learning modules were launched for all 
employees, enabling self-paced learning and fostering a 
culture of continuous development.~93 %
Employees Underwent 
Structured Training 
Empowering Focus and Well-being through Behavioural Workshops
AMGEN’s Achieve Program:  A Strategic Learning Intervention for Leadership 
Development
‘Achieve’ is a multiphase learning intervention 
designed to develop two core competencies: 
Achievement Orientation  and Agility . The 
program’s objective is to cultivate a growth mindset 
that enables leaders to manage change effectively 
and take full ownership of their goals. This initiative 
is also a key part of AMGEN’s leadership pipeline 
and succession planning.
Program Phases
 ®Assessment Phase
 »Conducted two tests: a psychometric 
assessment and a situational judgement test, 
followed by a behavioural interview to validate 
results. »A detailed report is generated for each participant, 
including strengths, development advice, and 
scores for the targeted competencies.
 ®Workshop
 »A 2-day in-house instructor-led workshop 
focused on developing Achievement Orientation 
and Agility using specific tools and techniques.
 ®Virtual Sustenance
 »Four virtual sustenance sessions are conducted 
by a leadership development coach, aiming 
to reinforce and apply the learning in the 
participants’ daily work schedules.

Empowering Teams through Training on PM 
Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana
As part of our proactive approach to enabling the 
success of the PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana, 
DNHDD Power Distribution Corporation Ltd. 
(DNHDDPDCL) partnered with the National Power 
Training Institute (NPTI)—a premier institute under 
the Ministry of Power—to build internal technical and 
customer-facing capabilities.
In November 2024, a two-day training program was 
conducted in Silvassa, focused on Grid-Connected 
Rooftop Solar Systems. The session was led by two 
expert trainers from NPTI. A total of 25 participants, 
including members of the Technical and Customer 
Service Teams from Daman and Silvassa, took part 
in the training. The agenda covered a comprehensive 
range of subjects essential for the successful 
implementation of the scheme:
 ®Introduction to PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana
 ®Overview of Solar Rooftop PV Systems
 ®Safety standards and best practices
 ®System design and site inspection procedures
 ®Grid connectivity and net metering protocols
 ®Administrative procedures and customer 
onboarding process
The sessions also included real-life scenarios and 
practical walkthroughs, equipping participants 
with an in-depth understanding of the end-to-
end process. The training was well-received, with 
participants appreciating the hands-on approach 
and the expertise of the trainers.
At the end of the program, all attendees were 
awarded certificates of completion, encouraging 
their readiness to support customers and accelerate 
adoption of the rooftop solar initiative.
This training initiative is a testament to the Company’s 
commitment to capacity building, technical 
excellence, and seamless customer service delivery 
in support of India’s clean energy transition.EMPLOYEES

objective was to build a transparent, scorecard-driven 
system that encouraged healthy competition, fostered 
engagement, and celebrated performance aligned with 
organisational values. Recognition was redefined—not 
just as an end-of-year ritual, but as an everyday practice 
woven into team culture.
Creating Positive Impact on Ground
The framework introduced multiple layers of recognition—
from ‘Shabash’  cards for daily contributions to quarterly 
and annual awards recognising innovation, safety, and extraordinary effort. Rewards include cash incentives, 
trophies, and appreciation certificates, with both teams 
and individuals acknowledged.
Since its rollout, the initiative has led to a visible uplift in 
morale, cross-functional collaboration, and ownership. 
Employees feel more engaged and appreciated, 
and leaders now have a tangible way to reinforce 
the behaviours that drive progress. By embedding 
appreciation into its performance culture, Torrent Power 
is building a more motivated, accountable, and future-
ready workforce.
Rewarding the Right Culture
At Torrent Power’s Distribution Units in Ahmedabad, Surat and Dahej, employee recognition was previously informal—
mostly verbal, often inconsistent. Though good performance was acknowledged in meetings, the absence of a 
structured system meant that meaningful appreciation was sporadic and often subjective.

Fostering a Culture of Quality, Safety  
and Sustainability
At Torrent Power, we are committed to fostering a culture 
of excellence and sustainability across our entire supply 
chain. We actively encourage our suppliers to adhere to the 
highest international standards by complying with ISO 9001 
(Quality Management System), ISO 14001 (Environmental 
Management System), and ISO 45001 (Occupational Health 
and Safety Management System). By aligning with these 
globally recognised standards, we ensure that our suppliers 
maintain superior quality in their processes, minimise their 
environmental impact, and prioritise the health and safety 
of their workforce. 
Enhancing Supplier Capabilities
To enhance supplier capabilities, we invest in their growth 
through comprehensive training programs focused on 
health, safety, and sustainability. In FY25, we conducted 
around 1,554 training sessions for our value chain partners 
covering safety protocols, energy efficiency, workplace 
ethics, and supply chain risk management, ensuring that our 
suppliers are well-equipped to meet the highest standards. 
These efforts aim to foster continuous improvement and 
resilience, enhancing both supplier capabilities and the 
overall sustainability and efficiency of our supply chain.
Supplier Code of Conduct
Our Supplier Code of Conduct ensures ethical business 
practices across the supply chain. Compliance with 
fair labour policies, environmental sustainability, and 
transparent sourcing is non-negotiable. All suppliers 
are required to adhere to minimum wage standards, 
enforce workplace safety, and uphold zero tolerance for 
corruption, child labour, and unfair business practices.  
We are committed to continuous improvement and collaborate 
closely with our suppliers to uphold these standards. 
Supplier Assessment and Performance 
Monitoring
We employ a comprehensive approach for screening 
and evaluating our suppliers. Our  structured evaluation 
process categorises suppliers based on their compliance 
with ESG and procurement policies. This process focuses 
on critical vendors, identified through 80:20 rule based on 
procurement value, enabling us to prioritise our suppliers 
who significantly contribute to our procurement activities. 
Our evaluation process begins with primary assessments 
conducted during the supplier registration phase. This 
initial step helps us gather essential information about 
potential suppliers. Following this, we conduct site visits 
to manufacturing facilities to perform in-depth evaluation. These visits allow us to verify the capabilities and practices of 
our suppliers. We also assess our suppliers’ environmental 
management systems through pre-determined criteria to 
ensure that our suppliers adhere to environmental standards 
and practices that align with our sustainability goals.
Supplier performance is monitored through a comprehensive 
framework that includes supervisor feedback, field 
force automation insights, internal and external audits, 
compliance monitoring systems, and Environment, Health 
& Safety (EHS) management surveys.
Our Commitment to Supplier 
Collaboration
We are dedicated to fostering strong, collaborative 
relationships with our suppliers through open communication 
and a two-way feedback channel. This ensures our suppliers 
are well-informed about our standards and allows us to 
benefit from their insights.
To enhance our relationships with suppliers and partners, 
we engage in regular collaboration through scheduled 
meetings, organised festival celebrations, and various 
get-together events. Annually, we host a vendor meet that 
brings together our suppliers and service providers. During 
this event, we share the Company’s strategies, initiatives, 
goals, targets, plans, and expectations to ensure seamless 
alignment. This includes areas such as statutory compliance, 
quality, health, safety, and environmental sustainability. 
We also actively seek feedback and suggestions from our 
vendors on these aspects, reinforcing our commitment to 
continuous improvement and mutual growth.

We believe that a robust and diverse supply chain is

Empowering Customers through  
QR-enabled Online Application Guide
In August 2024, the Company addressed a key 
customer service challenge, i.e. difficulty in navigating 
the online application registration process. This issue 
led to frequent dependence on customer support, 
resulting in reduced customer satisfaction and 
increased footfalls at service centres.
To address these issues, we developed a self-
explanatory process document in both English and 
Gujarati, detailing step-by-step instructions. This 
document eliminates the need for a Torrent employee 
to provide comprehensive guidance, empowering 
customers to utilise all features effectively. To 
improve accessibility, a QR code was integrated, 
allowing customers to instantly access the guide on 
their smartphones.
This initiative has boosted customer satisfaction, 
reduced walk-ins, minimised operational costs, 
and saved time for both customers and employees. 
By empowering users to complete applications 
independently, the Company has strengthened 
its brand credibility and streamlined the overall 
service process.

Empowering Students with Electrical Safety AwarenessDriving Efficiency through Paperless 
Refund System
In FY25, we implemented the Paperless Refund 
initiative at our Bhiwandi and SMK Distribution 
Franchise locations to streamline the refund process 
for permanently disconnected customers’ negative 
energy dues and cancelled application payments. 
Previously, the process was manual, involving 
physical voucher preparation, multiple approvals, 
and cheque issuance, which led to significant delays 
and inefficiencies.
To address these issues, we developed an online 
refund system in SAP to automate the process.  
This system automated the workflow, replacing 
manual steps with an online process, and enabled 
direct payments to consumers’ accounts. 
Additionally, it provided real-time tracking and 
thereby enhanced transparency.
Benefits
 ®Reduced Processing Time:  From 30 days to 
5 days.
 ®Increased Efficiency:  Eliminated manual steps 
and errors.
 ®Improved Satisfaction:  Faster refunds and better

Commitment to Data Protection
We prioritise and safeguard customer data with the 
utmost care, recognising the importance of protecting 
the personal information entrusted to us by our valued 
customers. To ensure customer data is protected, we take 
the following actions:
 ®Collect only essential customer data necessary to 
provide our services and enhance customer experience.
 ®Refrain from sharing customer data with third parties, 
except when mandated by law.
Our diligent efforts and robust security measures have 
successfully safeguarded customer data and maintained 
the integrity of our systems. We received no complaints of 
data breaches within our organisation during FY25.
Commitment to Excellence in Customer 
Service
At Torrent Power, we prioritise customer satisfaction and 
strive to exceed expectations through rigorous quality 
standards and continuous improvement. We continuously 
monitor and enhance our Customer Satisfaction (CSAT) 
score through surveys, feedback forms, and customer 
support interactions. In FY25, we received 41,839 
feedbacks, achieving a CSAT score of 94%. We listen to our customers, understand their needs, and incorporate their 
feedback into our decisions. This continuous feedback loop 
enables us to identify areas for improvement and address 
potential challenges efficiently. 
We also maintain high standards at our Plug Points through 
Mystery Shopping audits. In FY25, we achieved a quality 
score of 92%, reflecting our commitment to excellence. 
These evaluations help us refine customer interactions and 
ensure top-notch service at our Plug Points.

CSR Governance
We are committed to strong CSR governance to ensure 
effectiveness and accountability of our initiatives.
Corporate Social Responsibility and 
Sustainability (CSRS) Committee and Policy
At the board level, our Corporate Social Responsibility and 
Sustainability (CSRS) Committee oversees the Company’s 
community-facing initiatives. Our well-structured and 
holistic CSR policy outlines our focus areas, project 
categories, program types, delivery methodologies, and 
resources. It serves as a guiding principles for community 
engagement for all relevant employees and partners.
Annual Action Plan
The CSRS Committee convenes at least twice a year to 
develop an Annual Action Plan (AAP) that outlines selected 
projects, activities, and budgets for the year. After seeking 
board approval for the AAP, the Committee monitors its 
implementation and reviews the ongoing activities.Impact Measurement and Transparency
The Company consistently tracks the societal and 
environmental impact of its decisions, projects, and 
activities to identify areas for improvement and enhance 
trust with stakeholders.

Outreach activities
Our Outreach activities focus on reducing malnutrition & 
anaemia amongst children in the age – group of 6 months to 
6 years. Under this program, we organise baseline screening 
camps across various villages covered in two states including 
Gujarat, Maharashtra and Union Territory i.e., Diu, Daman and 
Dadra Nagar Haveli. Children are screened for anaemia and 
malnourishment and necessary interventions are done for 
possible improvement. Children identified as malnourished 
or anaemic or both are provided medical treatment and 
supplementary nutrition. The treatment plan for malnourished 
children is spread over a period of 3 months and anaemia 
treatment spans across 6 months. Our approach towards community healthcare initiatives basically comprises two distinct categories as under:

Medical services
Transforming Children’s Healthcare: UNM  Children 
Hospital and Paediatric Primary Health Centres (PHCs)
We employ a ‘hub and spoke’ model to deliver 
comprehensive healthcare to underprivileged children,  
particularly in remote areas. This model centers on UNM 
Children Hospital, the ‘hub’, and is supported by a network 
of UNM Children PHCs, the ‘spokes’.
 ®UNM Children PHCs
  In 2017, we started four paediatric centre in Sugen, 
Dahej, Indrad, and Balasinor of Gujarat with a focus on 
outpatient departments (OPDs) as ‘CARE’ measures. 
In 2020, we achieved a significant milestone by 
transforming the SUGEN paediatric centre into a 
150-bedded hospital, providing critical care to children. 
Consequently, 9 more PHCs have been started on daily 
basis at locations of Dediapada, Waghai, Naswadi, 
Radhanpur, Chhapi, Ankleshwar, Bhestan, Dholera, 
Junagadh to reach and serve people in interior rural 
areas deprived of quality affordable medical facilities. 
These centers provide essential primary paediatric 
care services. These services include free medical 
consultations, basic laboratory tests, and medications.
  Looking at the response from the community, we intend 
to establish a few more UNM Children PHCs at needy 
areas in Maharashtra and Gujarat in next year. ® UNM Children Hospital
  Located near Kamrej in Surat district, this 150-bedded, 
NABH & NABL- certified hospital, is fast emerging as a 
Centre of Excellence in Paediatric care. Established in 
2020, it offers advanced secondary and tertiary care, 
including complex surgeries across multiple specialties. 
The hospital is equipped with advanced technology and 
has implemented CMS and e-MRD systems to enhance 
operational efficiency. Cumulative status across all 12 UNM Children

Stories of Healing and Hope - Transforming Lives
Krishna’s Comeback: 
A New Life After 
Scoliosis01
Name:  Krishna Thakur
Age: 13 years
Location:  Khargone, Madhya Pradesh
Diagnosis:  Gait difficulties and scoliosis
Treatment:  Halo traction and scoliosis surgery
Born with abnormal gait, Krishna endured years of 
discomfort and limited mobility. His parents, after 
exhausting local options and physiotherapy, came to 
know about UNM Children Hospital through social 
media and brought him to Surat for evaluation. Doctors 
diagnosed severe spinal misalignment and recommended 
a staged approach: two months of halo traction followed 
by scoliosis surgery.
The treatment was a success. Krishna now walks with 
a straight back, sits comfortably for long hours, and 
even rides a bicycle. From struggling to stand upright 
to studying confidently in the 8th grade, Krishna’s 
transformation makes UNM Children Hospital team proud 
of the achievement and exemplifies the life-changing 
impact of early diagnosis and expert care.Name:  Hayan Hirenbhai Vora
Age: 3 years
Location:  Olpad, Gujarat
Diagnosis:  Brachial Plexus Injury
Treatment:  Microsurgical repair, nerve transfer, 
hand reconstruction
After a normal pregnancy, Hayan was born with a severe 
brachial plexus injury, limiting the function of his right 
arm. His family tried various hospitals, spending over ₹1 
Lakh, but saw little improvement. Referred to UNMCH, 
Hayan was evaluated by a plastic surgeon who diagnosed 
the extent of nerve damage and planned a complex 
microsurgical intervention.
The surgery was successfully completed, ushering in a 
tailored program of post-operative care and rehabilitation. 
Hayan’s hand movements gradually improved, and with 
regular follow-ups, his parents now see steady progress.  
His recovery shows how compassionate, expert-led care 
can reverse even complex congenital conditions.

=== page 111 ===
Name:  Fenil Chandrakant Mistry
Age:  6 years
Location:  Surat, Gujarat
Diagnosis: Moyamoya Disease
Treatment:  Endoscopic Assisted Micro-Surgery 
(EDAMS)
While en-route to school, Fenil suddenly collapsed–an 
alarming episode that led doctors to suspect a stroke 
from a blocked brain artery. Local hospitals quoted 
surgery costs of ₹2 Lakh, an expense far beyond the 
family’s reach. When admitted to UNM Children Hospital, 
specialists identified Moyamoya disease, a rare and 
progressive cerebrovascular disorder.
Fenil underwent Endoscopic Assisted Micro-Surgery 
(EDAMS) at UNM Children Hospital to restore brain blood 
flow. The procedure went off without a hitch, and Fenil’s 
recovery was remarkably swift. Within days, he stabilised, 
resumed eating, and began interacting normally with 
family and friends. His experience underscores how 
prompt diagnosis and access to advanced, affordable 
care can be truly life-changing.Name:  Shivansh (B/o Runadevi)
Age:  Newborn
Location:  Surat urban, Gujarat
Diagnosis:  Extreme prematurity (25 weeks), weight: 700g
Treatment: 91-day NICU care, ventilatory support, 
blood transfusions
Born at just 25 weeks and weighing 700 grams, Shivansh’s 
chances of survival were slim. Private NICU care would 
have cost over ₹14–15 Lakhs—an impossible sum for 
his family. Referred to UNM Children Hospital’s NICU, 
Shivansh received round-the-clock critical care, including 
ventilator support, antibiotics, and multiple transfusions.
Despite multiple life-threatening complications, including 
Apnea, Sepsis, and Hypoglycaemia, the NICU team 
persisted. Emotional counselling and support helped 
the parents through each hurdle. After 91 days in the 
NICU, Shivansh was finally discharged—healthy, 
stable, and ready to go home. His recovery filled the 
UNM Children’s Hospital team with immense pride, 
satisfaction, and renewed motivation. His journey 
stands as a testament to how specialised neonatal 
care and steadfast resilience can help even the 
tiniest fighters triumph against overwhelming odds.

Strategic Shift to Advanced Surgical Care
In 2022, advancing UNM Children Hospital towards a Centre of Excellence, we took a strategic decision 
to shift focus from general OPD and IPD services to specialised surgical interventions, addressing the 
growing need for complex paediatric surgeries. Combined with state-of-the-art facilities and a team of 
expert clinicians, this transformation has made UNM Children’s Hospital a premier paediatric referral centre.

Future Roadmap
As Shiksha Setu enters FY26, the program stands at 
a pivotal stage of scaling with depth. With expanded 
reach across 117 schools, the emphasis will now focus 
on consolidating program quality. The coming year’s 
strategy will prioritise impact and scale both, ensuring that every program touchpoint is not just delivered, but 
meaningfully translated into improved learning, inclusion, 
and opportunity for every child and community we serve.
Project Saksham - Empowering Women through Skill Development
In the rural areas of Indrad, Kadi Taluka, Mehsana District, women often have limited opportunities for 
self-improvement and economic empowerment. Project Saksham aims to address this by providing skill 
development and entrepreneurship training.
The project offers a free, three-month sewing training course, covering garment-making, entrepreneurship, 
financial literacy, and market management. Local stakeholders, including the Gram Panchayat and Anganwadi 
workers, help mobilise community participation.
The program provides women with the skills and confidence to start tailoring businesses, leading to improved 
financial independence, enhanced entrepreneurial and tailoring skills, and increased self-esteem.
Nikitaben's Journey to Financial  Independence
Nikitaben Udaji Thakor, a 20-year-old from Indrad 
village, lived in a joint family and had limited 
opportunities despite completing her 10th grade 
education. Her husband's low income and family's 
financial struggles, compounded by her uncle’s 
alcohol addiction, caused significant distress. Project 
Saksham offered a chance for change. Nikitaben 
enrolled in the sewing program, mastered garment-
making, and gained entrepreneurial confidence. 
With a sewing machine purchased by her father, she 
started her own business, selling stitched garments 
in nearby villages. Overcoming initial hesitations 
about door-to-door sales, she now earns a monthly 
income of ₹3,000–₹3,500, inspiring other women in 
her community.Chandrikaben’s Path to Self-Reliance
Chandrikaben Vijaybhai Thakor, a 31-year-old mother 
of two from Kadi district, also found empowerment 
through Project Saksham. Her husband worked 
as a rickshaw driver, and her father-in-law ran a 
small grocery shop. Despite family responsibilities, 
Chandrikaben was determined to learn and grow. 
The sewing centre provided her with new skills, 
increased her confidence, and earned her family’s 
trust. She learned to make various garments and 
received training in entrepreneurship, financial 
literacy, and market management. After completing 
the training, she started sewing blouses for villagers 
and now earns ₹2,500 to ₹3,000 per month. 
Chandrikaben views this as just the beginning and 
aspires to expand her business, expressing deep 
gratitude to Project Saksham for the transformative 
knowledge and self-confidence it provided.COMMUNITIES

UJAAS: Illuminating Lives of Senior Citizens 
Throughout the years, the Torrent Group has been dedicated to enhancing societal well-being through various impactful 
initiatives. In honour of our Founder, Shri U. N. Mehta’s birth centenary, we launched a program called UJAAS. Recognising 
the increasing challenge of social isolation among senior citizens, we initiated support for old-age homes, fostering a sense 
of belonging and purpose among them through:
 ®Providing quality care and emotional support,  
ensuring that elderly residents receive the attention and 
compassion they need.
 ®Companionship programs  including cultural events, 
festive celebrations, national day celebrations, organising 
games and various other interactive engagements.
 ®Regular health check-ups and wellness camps 
including yoga/meditation workshops,  to monitor 
and improve the health of senior citizens.
 ®Cultural and recreational outings  to enhance social 
interaction, such as temple visits and theatre outings. 
These outings provide opportunities for seniors to 
engage with the community and enjoy new experiences. ®Infrastructure improvements  to meet specific needs 
and offer essential amenities like medicines and clothing. 
Upgrading facilities to ensure a comfortable and safe 
living environment.
This initiative aims to improve emotional well-being, social 
inclusion, and the quality of life for elderly residents, 
reinforcing our commitment to compassionate and 
sustainable social impact. By establishing connections, 
offering new experiences, and supporting their mental 
and emotional health, we create a positive and fulfiling 
environment for the elderly.

Emission Management Initiatives
The Company has adopted a comprehensive approach to emissions management, implementing a range of strategic 
initiatives aimed at reducing its environmental footprint. Key measures undertaken include:
Energy Efficiency Enhancements
Continuous efforts are made to reduce auxiliary power 
consumption and optimise station heat rates. These efforts 
enhance energy efficiency, minimise emissions, lower 
operational costs, and improve the overall performance of 
our thermal plants. 
Energy Conservation at Generation units
Efforts are made to conserve energy in our operations 
through optimising fuel blending and combustion, 
optimisation of air compressor operation, circulating water 
pumps operation, unit startup time reduction, etc.
Reduction in Distribution Losses
Efforts are made to improve efficiency of power distribution 
networks to reduce electricity losses, thereby lowering 
emissions and reliance on diesel generators. To improve 
distribution networks, inefficient distribution transformers 
were replaced, illegal networks were taken down, 
predictive monitoring was integrated, outage analysis was 
conducted, and preventive maintenance was performed on 
Distribution Substations. Sustainable Practices
We have implemented energy-efficient technologies, 
adopting energy-saving standard operating procedures 
(SOPs) & protocols. These includes digital initiatives, such 
as e-billing, Field Force Application for field workforce 
and processing of payments through online modes (now 
at >86% adoption), to reduce paper consumption and 
waste generation.
Rooftop Solar Installation
Installed solar panels across various company premises, 
enabling captive generation of 6,696 GJ of clean energy 
and reducing reliance on fossil fuel-based electricity.

Water Stewardship: A Commitment to Sustainability
At the heart of our operations lies a steadfast commitment 
to responsible water stewardship. Our initiatives are 
designed to enhance water usage efficiency and promote 
environmental sustainability, ensuring that we contribute 
positively to the communities and ecosystems we serve.
Our strategy focuses on conserving freshwater through 
innovative management practices, infrastructure upgrades, 
and technology integration. By reducing consumption, maximising reuse, and enhancing sustainability, we aim to 
set new standards in water stewardship.
We have implemented Zero Liquid Discharge solutions 
across our generation units to ensure minimal water 
wastage. By tracking water consumption at each plant 
and setting reduction targets, we are committed to 
continuous improvement.
Reducing Consumption
Our dedication to reducing water consumption has led to implementation of several measures across our facilities:
 ®Advanced leak detection systems have been deployed 
to minimise water loss.
 ®At SUGEN, we have implemented measures to reuse 
water from sampling systems of the demineralisation 
plant and control losses in the water-steam cycle.
 ®By maximising dry ash utilisation and reusing ash pond 
water at AMGEN, we have further reduced water usage.
 ®By implementing effective ash pond water utilisation, 
AMGEN unit reduced annual freshwater usage by 
53,475 m³. ®At our gas-based units, we have significantly reduced 
service water consumption by using high-pressure jet 
spray pumps for filter washing.
 ®Drip Irrigation Systems has been implemented at various 
locations, these systems not only save water but also 
reduce labour costs.
 ®We have introduced robotic cleaning for water tanks, 
enhancing efficiency and hygiene. 
 ®We have expanded the deployment of robotic dry-
cleaning systems across various solar plants. This 
initiative has enabled us to conserve up to 5,013 kl of 
water annually.

Rainwater Harvesting for Sustainable Water Management
At AMGEN, a rainwater harvesting system was 
implemented at the E Unit Water Treatment Plant building 
shed to enhance water conservation. Previously, rainwater 
collected at the shed was directed to the stormwater 
drainage system due to Central Pollution Control Board 
(CPCB) regulations that restrict groundwater recharge on 
industrial premises, leading to the under-utilisation of a 
valuable water resource. 
To address this challenge, AMGEN devised an alternative 
method to effectively utilise the rainwater within the plant’s 
operational framework. Rainwater is now collected from 
the building’s terrace and transported through a piping 
network to the storage clear well sump. The Water Treatment Plant building shed was identified as the most suitable 
location due to existing infrastructure, including storage and 
pumping systems, allowing for efficient implementation.  
The stored rainwater is then pumped and reused for various 
non-potable purposes within the plant and for irrigation.
Key Impact:
 ®A sustainable and cost-effective water management 
solution utilising existing infrastructure was achieved.
 ®The potential for rooftop rainwater harvesting is 
approximately 712 kl per annum, based on an average 
annual rainfall of 582 mm and a shed area of 1,530 m².

Responsible Waste Management for a 
Cleaner Tomorrow
We are committed to environmental sustainability, 
particularly through comprehensive waste management 
practices that embody the principles of the circular 
economy. By adhering to the 3Rs—Reduce, Reuse, and 
Recycle—we strive to minimise waste generation, optimise 
resource utilisation, and implement sustainable disposal 
methods across our operations. 
We strictly adhere to all regulations concerning the safe 
handling, transportation, and disposal of hazardous 
waste. Our robust protocols ensure that hazardous 
materials are managed responsibly, minimising any 
potential environmental impact. To maintain transparency 
and accountability, we meticulously document waste 
generation in separate waste passbooks, updated monthly.  
This diligent record-keeping allows us to track our progress 
and continuously enhance our waste management practices.
Waste Management Strategy
Our waste management approach encompasses:
Responsible Utilisation
Efficient use of resources is paramount for sustainable 
development. One of the key strategies to achieve this is 
by preventing waste generation at the source. By adopting 
processes that emphasise optimal resource utilisation 
and asset reuse, we have diminished the demand for new 
resources and significantly reduce waste. For example, 
implementing processes for reusing Mini Section Pillars 
(MSPs) and meter boxes which are recovered from sites 
and are in good condition, can significantly reduce the need 
for new resources and minimise waste. To minimise material 
wastage and enhance quality control, we have established 
in-house testing infrastructure that evaluates materials prior 
to installation. This proactive approach reduces the risk of 
failure and wastage of resources. 
We also prioritise the use of environmentally friendly 
materials and technologies across our operations. To 
reduce environmental impact and enhance efficiency, we 
have adopted dry-type transformers and SF₆ insulated 
switchgears, which eliminate the risk of oil leakage 
associated with conventional oil-filled transformers/ 
switchgears. To further support eco-friendly operations, 
our transformers now feature corrugated fin radiator 
designs, which enhance cooling efficiency while reducing 
material consumption compared to conventional designs. 
The use of recycled paper is encouraged for billing and 
other stationery purposes. Additionally, our major solar 
units have received Single-Use Plastic Free Certification, reinforcing our commitment to phasing out single-use 
plastics and validating biodegradable alternatives aimed 
at waste reduction.
Effective Segregation 
We have implemented streamlined processes to separate 
different waste types, which is crucial for ensuring 
appropriate handling and disposal. This involves diligent 
segregation of e-waste, hazardous waste, plastic waste, 
etc. Additionally, strategically placed, color-coded bins 
are used to promote efficient waste segregation. Clearly 
marked areas are designated for the safe storage and 
handling of hazardous and other waste types until disposal. 
Sustainable Disposal Methods
We are committed to reducing landfill contributions and 
environmental impact through eco-friendly practices.  
Our waste management practices include:
 ®Maximising Waste Recovery through Recycling and 
Composting:  We actively divert waste from landfills 
through comprehensive recycling and composting 
programs. For example, food and horticultural waste 
is processed into nutrient-rich compost, supporting 
circular economy principles.
 ®Responsible Disposal via Authorised Recyclers:  
Hazardous waste—including used oils, batteries, 
e-waste and biomedical waste—is managed in strict Hazardous wasteOrganic waste

16.  Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR)
  The CSR Activities undertaken by the Company were 
under the thrust areas of Community Healthcare, 
Education & Knowledge Enhancement and Social care 
& concern. During the year, the Company was required 
to spend I 45.55	Crore	(2%	of	the	average	net	profit	of	
the	past	three	financial	years).	The	total	amount	spent	
during the year was I 54.63 Crore (including surplus of 
154
Torrent Power Limited
=== page 158 ===
I 1.47 Crore arising at implementing agency level from 
temporary investment of funds for FY25). Further, the 
unspent amount at the end of the year was transferred 
to Unspent CSR Account of related ongoing projects 
by the Company. The brief details of the major CSR 
activities are described hereunder:
1)  REACH:  Driven by the belief of Chairman Emeritus, 
Sudhir Mehta ‘Children are the future of our nation 
and this future must be well preserved’, the	flagship	
CSR program of the Group REACH – Reach EAch 
CHild was initiated in the year 2016 under the aegis of 
UNM Foundation, a Section 8 Company (UNMF).
  In the past years, UNMF adjusted its approach towards 
community healthcare initiatives, which are now 
carried out in two distinct categories viz. Outreach 
Activities and Medical Services.
 Outreach Activities
  Our Outreach activities focus on reducing malnutrition & 
anemia amongst children in the age – group of 6 months 
to 6 years. Under this programme, we organise baseline 
screening camps across various villages covered in 
two states including Gujarat, Maharashtra and Union 
Territory i.e., Diu, Daman and Dadra Nagar Haveli. 
Children are screened for anemia and malnourishment; 
necessary interventions are done for possible 
improvement. Children identified as malnourished 
or anaemic or both are provided medical treatment 
and supplementary nutrition. The treatment plan for 
malnourished children is spread over a period of 3 
months and anemia treatment spans across 6 months.
